name: 01 Faber GTAA trend
notes: 5 ETFs (SPY EFA IEF VNQ DBC), 20% each when above its N-month SMA at month end, else SHY. Faber (2007/2013).
verdict: Works mainly as drawdown control (max DD -11% vs SPY -34%); lags SPY's return in the 2015-26 bull market. PBO high: the 6 vs 10 month choice is noise.

name: 02 Time series momentum
notes: 9 ETFs, long if trailing return > 0, inverse-volatility sized to a target, rest in SHY, no leverage. Moskowitz-Ooi-Pedersen (2012), Hurst-Ooi-Pedersen (2017).
verdict: Steady, low volatility, Sharpe 0.78 out of sample. Low return on its own; a good portfolio building block.

name: 03 Keller VAA dual momentum
notes: Offensive SPY EFA EEM AGG, defensive LQD IEF SHY, monthly. Keller & Keuning VAA-G4 (2017); 12m score = Antonacci-style dual momentum.
verdict: Decayed after publication (out-of-sample Sharpe 0.51, deflated Sharpe below 0.9). Superseded by HAA (#14).

name: 04 Crypto Donchian trend BTC
notes: Average of Donchian breakout states (enter above N-day high, exit below N/2-day low), volatility targeted, max 100%. After Zarattini-Pagani-Barbon (2025).
verdict: 19.9%/yr vs 36.2% for holding BTC, but the drawdown is -34% instead of -77% and the Sharpe is a bit higher (0.88 vs 0.82). Setting choice is fragile (PBO 0.67), so expect less.

name: 05 VIX term structure SVXY
notes: Long SVXY when VIX/VIX3M < threshold (contango), optional VIX > 10d realised vol filter, else cash. Simon-Campasano (2014), Zarattini-Aziz-Mele (2025).
verdict: Simple SVXY contango rule: -50% drawdowns, Sharpe 0.36 out of sample. Don't run it.

name: 06 Connors RSI2 index ETFs
notes: SPY QQQ IWM DIA: buy at the close when RSI(2) < X and close > 200d SMA, sell at the close above the 5d SMA. Connors & Alvarez (2008).
verdict: Connors RSI(2) has decayed: out-of-sample Sharpe 0.36, -41% drawdown. Matches the published re-tests.

name: 07 IBS mean reversion
notes: SPY QQQ IWM DIA: buy at the close when IBS < X, sell at a close above yesterday's high or IBS > 0.8. Pagonidis (2013).
verdict: Best single bot. Works on each ETF separately (QQQ Sharpe 1.14, SPY 0.94, ~340 trades each, ~72% winners) and still works when filled at the next open (Sharpe 0.76).

name: 08 Overnight after down days
notes: SPY QQQ: buy market-on-close after N down closes, sell at the next open. Overnight-return literature (Cooper-Cliff-Gulen 2008, Lou-Polk-Skouras 2019).
verdict: Clean but tiny edge (~2.4%/yr, -7% DD). Only the 3-down-day version works; the 1-day default does not. Useful as a diversifier.

name: 09 Turn of the month SPY
notes: Hold SPY from the close N trading days before month end to the close of trading day M of the new month. Lakonishok-Smidt (1988), McConnell-Xu (2008).
verdict: The turn-of-month effect still exists on SPY (63% winning months, profit factor 1.8). Holding 5 days before month end works better than the classic 1.

name: 10 Sector momentum rotation
notes: 9 SPDR sectors, hold the top K by N-month return, monthly; IEF when SPY < 200d SMA. Moskowitz-Grinblatt (1999) industry momentum.
verdict: Decent (8.8%/yr, Sharpe 0.69) but deflated Sharpe 0.84: could be luck. Not proven.

name: 11 FX trend majors
notes: 7 USD majors, long/short vs N-day SMA, inverse-vol sized, weekly. Spot only: carry (interest differential) NOT included.
verdict: FX trend on majors lost money 2015-26, as the research warned (post-publication Sharpe near zero). Spot only, carry not included.

name: 12 Lower band IBS SPY QQQ
notes: Quantitativo (2024) mean reversion: close below (10d high - 2.5 x 25d avg range) and IBS < 0.3, exit above yesterday's high.
verdict: Strong (Sharpe 0.88, in the market 11% of days) but sensitive to fill timing: Sharpe 0.56 if filled at the next open. Needs market-on-close orders.

name: 13 Your MACD 12-144-9 dip rule
notes: The earlier sessions' MACD(12,144,9) cross-up-below-zero rule, daily bars, 12 big tech names, max 3 positions. Survivorship bias: the names are today's winners.
verdict: Your MACD 12/144/9 rule exactly as specified LOSES (-1.2%/yr out of sample). The optimiser's pick (12/26/9, no filter, 60 days) made 21%/yr but simply holding the same 12 stocks made 36%/yr, and the list is today's winners (survivorship bias). Not recommended.

name: 14 Keller HAA
notes: Hybrid Asset Allocation (Keller 2023): TIP canary, top 4 of 8 by 1/3/6/12m momentum, else IEF/cash. Rules read from allocatesmartly.com.
verdict: Strong new find: 10%/yr, Sharpe 0.98, max DD -13% out of sample; the published setting was also the plateau pick (PBO 0.16).

name: 15 Volatility Edge VIX
notes: Zarattini-Aziz-Mele (2025) Strategy 4: short vol (SVXY) sized VIX/100 in contango with positive VRP, half size with negative VRP, long VIXY in backwardation.
verdict: Works only WITHOUT the paper's long-VIX leg (Sharpe 0.67, DD -8%). The paper's exact version: Sharpe 0.54, DD -30%.

name: 16 Connors Double 7s
notes: Short Term Trading Strategies That Work (Connors & Alvarez 2008): buy a 7-day closing low above the 200d SMA, sell a 7-day closing high.
verdict: Double 7s has decayed: Sharpe 0.47, -36% drawdown, and walk-forward Sharpe 0.28.

name: 17 Crypto trend top coins
notes: Donchian ensemble across BTC ETH BNB XRP ADA DOGE SOL, vol targeted, equal risk. After Zarattini-Pagani-Barbon (2025) 'Catching Crypto Trends'.
verdict: Good on paper (12.7%/yr, Sharpe 1.16 vs BTC 0.50, DD -17%) but the coin list is today's survivors, which flatters it. Kept out of the portfolio.
